ORDER Assailing the award dated 31/1/2012passed by Member, 4th Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Morena in Claim Case No. 87/2010 on the point of inadequacy of the compensation, the appellant has preferred this appeal for enhancement of award under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

entities.text: 4th Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Morena
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The accident in question took place on 25/9/2009 in which the appellant sustained grievous injuries and fractures in right leg and head.

2. Appellant/claimant had filed the claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 seeking compensation to the tune of Rs. 10,60,000/- for the bodily injuries and fractures suffered by appellant/claimant in the accident which took place on 25/9/2009.
However, Claims Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.2,25,000/- with interest at the rate of 7% per annum from the date of application.

3. Briefly stated facts of the case are that on 25/9/2009 at about 10.30 pm when appellant alongwith companions was going on their bicycles from NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:13596 2 MA-496-2012 Morena to their village, it is alleged that near powerhouse, due to rash and negligent driving of jeep driver No. MP30T0132, jeep dashed his bicycle, due to which he suffered grievous hurts in his head, legs and other parts of body.
He suffered fracture in right leg and in head and also lost his voice and suffered permanent disability.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Shri Gupta, learned counsel representing the appellant, contends that the injuries sustained by the appellant were grievous in nature.

The appellant suffered severe bodily injuries alongwith fracture in right leg and head and thereby suffered permanent disability to the extent of 60% in right leg; whereas, Claims Tribunal only assessed permanent disability to the extent of 30%.

The Claims Tribunal has only assessed the incomes of injured Rs. 3,000/- whereas, he used to earn Rs.
5,000/-per month..

Further, the amount of award under the heads medical expenses, grievous injury, Special diet and pain and suffering which is on the lower side, thus the compensation awarded by the learned Tribunal is inadequate, without looking to the nature of grievous injuries sustained, hospitalization and medical bills.
In view of the foregoing submissions, the enhancement of the compensation so awarded by the Tribunal, has been prayed for.
5. On the other hand, Shri Sharma, learned counsel representing the respondent/Insurance Company, supported the impugned award and prayed for dismissal of the appeal.

6. After having heard learned counsel appearing for the parties and on perusal of the pleadings and the evidence so adduced, in the opinion of this Court, considering the nature of injuries especially fractures sustained, treatment papers and its period, the mental pain and suffering and also the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:13596 3 MA-496-2012 other heads, the compensation as awarded by the Claims Tribunal is liable to be enhanced by Rs. 1,60,000/- in lump sum thereby making the total compensation Rs. 3,85,000/- which shall be paid within two months from today.
7. In view of the forgoing discussions, the appeal succeeds and is hereby allowed in part.
The appellant is held entitled to receive the enhanced amount of Rs. 1,60,000/- in addition to the amount of compensation already awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
The enhanced amount shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing claim case.
The other conditions as imposed by claims Tribunal including the liability shall remain intact.
8. With the aforesaid modification in the impugned award, the appeal stands allowed in part.

(ROOPESH CHANDRA VARSHNEY) JUDGE JPS/-
JAI PRAKASH SOLANKI 2024.08.20 14:38:11 +05'30'
